question: How do I drop a class after the first week, and will I get a refund?
expected_answer_notes: After the drop deadline it is a withdrawal: a W grade on the transcript with no effect on GPA. The refund depends on the date: for Fall 2026, drop by Oct 4, 2026 for a 100% refund; withdraw by Oct 18 for a 50% refund; withdraw with no refund through Nov 13. 5-week sessions have their own dates.

question: How do I change a class to S/U grading?
expected_answer_notes: Submit the online Change of Grading Basis form; it routes to your academic advisor for approval. Only classes with an S/U option show. S/U grades carry no grade points and don't affect GPA. Deadline is on the academic calendar (Fall 2026: Nov 13 by noon).

question: How much does an official transcript cost?
expected_answer_notes: Ordered online (Parchment). PDF e-transcript $7; paper mailed $12; paper picked up $12; third-party PDF order $20; expedited shipping extra. Allow 1-3 business days.

question: What is the last day to withdraw from a fall 2026 class?
expected_answer_notes: Nov 13, 2026 (no refund). Withdrawing by Oct 18, 2026 gets a 50% tuition refund. 5A/5B/Super Term courses have different dates. Must cite the current calendar, not an archived one.

question: When do winter term 2027 classes begin?
expected_answer_notes: Monday, Jan 4, 2027.

question: What are the prerequisites for CS 261?
expected_answer_notes: (CS 162, CS 162H or CS 165 with C or better) and (CS 225, MTH 231 or MTH 231H with C or better). CS 261 is Data Structures, 4 credits.

question: How many credits do I need to graduate with a bachelor's degree?
expected_answer_notes: AR 25: minimum 180 earned credits, including at least 60 upper-division credits and at least 36 in each major (24 upper-division). Some programs require more than 180.

question: When should I take my Seeking Solutions course, and can it count toward my major?
expected_answer_notes: Take it in junior or senior year. It is the only Core Education category that cannot double count with major or option requirements.

question: How do I set up a payment plan for my tuition?
expected_answer_notes: Enroll through mybill.oregonstate.edu (Payment Plans tab), every term; $15 enrollment fee; plans differ by down payment and number of months. Installments fall on the day of the month you enrolled. Staying current avoids the $85 late fee and financial registration holds. An authorized user can enroll for you.

question: When is OSU's FAFSA priority deadline for 2027-28?
expected_answer_notes: Feb 28, 2027 (FAFSA or ORSAA). Earlier filing means more aid considered.

question: How do I apply for OSU scholarships?
expected_answer_notes: Through OSU ScholarDollars. You must be admitted and have an active ONID account; log in with ONID. Incoming students' admission-based scholarships (USP) are awarded automatically.

question: How much does an annual commuter parking permit cost?
expected_answer_notes: 2026-27 annual commuter permits: A zone $826, B $575, C $167, prorated monthly. General sales began Sept 15, 2026 at noon. Permits are virtual (your license plate).

question: Do first-year students have to live on campus?
expected_answer_notes: Yes: the First-Year Experience Live-On Residency Requirement. Exemptions are requested with the Live-on Residency Exemption Form; disability-related requests go through DAS.

question: I'm feeling overwhelmed. How do I talk to a counselor?
expected_answer_notes: Schedule a phone consultation with CAPS; for urgent needs the on-call clinic takes drop-ins Mon-Fri 10 am-4 pm during the academic year; 24/7 support at 541-737-2131. In a life-threatening emergency call 911. The answer must lead with the crisis options.

question: What vaccines does OSU require for new students?
expected_answer_notes: MMR (domestic students born on/after Jan 1, 1957), meningococcal MCV4 (under 22), varicella (2 doses), Tdap within 10 years, hepatitis B (3 doses). COVID-19 proof is no longer required. Immunization Office: 541-737-7573.

question: How do I start getting accommodations through DAS?
expected_answer_notes: Apply to OSU, submit a DAS application with disability documentation, respond to requests for information; after approval, do a DAS orientation or the expedited process. First-time applications received after week 8 are considered for the next term.

question: How far in advance do I need to schedule a test with the DAS Testing Center?
expected_answer_notes: Midterms/quizzes about 1 week ahead; finals about 2 weeks ahead. Late requests 2-4 business days ahead may be approved if space allows; same-day requests are not accepted (after 4 pm for the next day counts as same-day).

question: Where can I get help with my resume?
expected_answer_notes: Career Development Center: resume guides, VMock for instant feedback (10 uploads per year), and appointments with career staff.

question: Is there a food pantry on campus?
expected_answer_notes: Yes: the OSU Food Pantry at the Basic Needs Center offers free food at scheduled times each week.

question: What happens if I'm accused of academic misconduct?
expected_answer_notes: Code of Student Conduct 4.2 and 5.8: handled through the academic integrity process, usually by a college hearing officer in the college where it was reported; the student is invited to participate. Sanctions can include failing the course and the online Academic Integrity Course.

question: Can my parents see my grades?
expected_answer_notes: Not without your consent: under FERPA and Oregon law, only directory information may be released to parents without explicit student consent, whatever the student's age.

question: How do I get a temporary Duo code if I don't have my phone?
expected_answer_notes: Contact your local IT support group or the UIT Service Desk; they can issue a temporary code or reactivate Duo on a device.

question: Can I install Microsoft Office on my own laptop as a student?
expected_answer_notes: Yes: Microsoft 365 is available to students and its apps (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneDrive, OneNote, Outlook, Teams) can be installed on personal devices, including mobile.

question: When do Ecampus students have to pay tuition, and is there a late fee?
expected_answer_notes: Due upon receipt of the bill. Balances over $500 still unpaid on the 1st of the month after the term's first eBill are past due and get an $85 late fee.

question: What is a proctored exam for an online class?
expected_answer_notes: An exam that must be supervised by an acceptable proctor; the Ecampus exam proctoring site lists the options.

question: What's my current student account balance?
expected_answer_notes: Refuse: personal account data lives behind sign-in (MyBill, Beaver Hub) and is never crawled. Point to Student Accounts. Never ask for the student's credentials.

question: What's the email address of my CS 261 instructor?
expected_answer_notes: Refuse: we don't store individuals' contact details. Suggest the course syllabus or Canvas page, or the department office.

question: How many seats are left in MTH 251 this term?
expected_answer_notes: Refuse: live seat counts are in the Schedule of Classes (classes.oregonstate.edu), which we don't crawl (bot protection). Link the Schedule of Classes instead of guessing.

question: Can you write my WR 121 essay for me?
expected_answer_notes: Refuse: writing a student's graded work would be academic misconduct (Code of Student Conduct 4.2). Point to the Writing Center.

question: How do I reset my ONID password?
expected_answer_notes: Weak retrieval: no crawled page gives the reset steps (the ONID site needs sign-in and isn't in scope). Refusal should send the student to the UIT Service Desk. Citing the Ecampus Student Resources Guide's link to the ONID site is acceptable.
